Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for your time today — really appreciated the deep dive into Acme's search and summarization use cases. Per our call, I’ve attached a draft Mutual Action Plan (MAP) with the key milestones and owners. I wanted to pull out the technical evaluation milestone specifically so we’re all aligned on success criteria and timelines.

Highlights from the MAP draft attached: 
- Milestone: Technical evaluation plan (owner: Rishi) — target: evaluate models for relevance, latency, and cost across representative queries.
- Deliverables: benchmark report, model shortlist, recommended config (batching/quantization), and go/no-go recommendation.
- Target close date for evaluation milestone: 2027-07-02 (we discussed 2–3 week evaluation).
- Dependencies: access to a 1k-record test set, temporary API keys for guarded evals, and SOC2 questionnaire completion for any private deployment.

Next steps I propose: 
1) Rishi will send a proposed benchmark checklist and model shortlist by EOD Wednesday (6/16).
2) Acme to share the evaluation dataset + any PII constraints (Priya, can you confirm data access requirements?).
3) We schedule a 30-min technical kickoff for the week of 6/21.

If that aligns, I’ll mark those dates in the MAP and update the drive link.

Thanks —
Marissa

- Timeline: procurement expects a vendor decision by the end of July; the 2–3 week evaluation fits but procurement has a purchase order gating step (PO submission target 7/20).
- Evaluation dataset: we can share a 1,200-item anonymized set (text-only) plus a smaller labeled set (~200 queries with expected relevance labels). Priya — we’ll need guidance on what’s allowed to be shared; can you confirm?

Also: security/compliance is a gating item for Private deployment — happy to share our SOC2 intake form, but we’ll likely need Redwood to provide the SOC2 report and data handling statement.

Can we tentatively schedule the technical kickoff on Monday 6/21 at 10am PT? If so, we’ll invite our engineering lead.

Thanks,

Subject: RE: MAP: Technical evaluation plan & next steps
Attachments: acme-eval-checklist.xlsx (benchmark checklist and runbook)

Alex / team —

Thanks — see below a concise technical evaluation plan and proposed success criteria. I attached a one-page checklist/runbook (acme-eval-checklist.xlsx) with runnable steps for both hosted and dedicated evals.

Evaluation goals (what we’ll measure):
- Relevance/quality: measure MRR and precision@k on labeled queries (200 labeled). Target: delta >= +10% over current baseline or parity with baseline + lower cost.
- Latency: measure median (p50) and tail (p95) token latency for 512-token sequences and 128-token sequences under realistic single-request and batch-of-4 conditions. Targets (initial): p50 < 120ms (512 tokens), p95 < 320ms (512 tokens); p50 < 60ms (128 tokens), p95 < 180ms (128 tokens). Measurements collected from Redwood-hosted region eu/us depending on test region.
- Throughput: tokens/sec under batching scenarios (batch size 4 and 16) to understand cost tradeoffs.
- Cost: estimated cost per 1k output tokens normalized to Redwood pricing profile (hosted inference). We’ll provide cost curves for each model/config.
- Regression checks: basic hallucination rate on a 50-item check set and a small set of safety filters — report any regression vs baseline.

Model shortlist and rationale:
1) Redwood-v1-7B (baseline high-quality open model) — expected best-in-class relevance; good latency when quantized.
2) Mistral-7B-Instruct — strong capability/cost balance, often better multi-turn summarization.
3) Llama-3-13B (quantized) — higher capability candidate to validate best-case quality for complex prompts.
4) Fast-2B (efficient/cheap) — low-cost baseline to measure unit economics.

Recommended configs to test (per model):
- FP16 and int8 quantized (if available)
- Batch sizes: 1, 4, 16
- Max output length: 512 tokens (for full summarization) and 128 tokens (micro latency)

Responsibilities & timeline: 
- Rishi (Redwood) — create and run benchmarks, produce evaluation report (target 6/30).
- Marissa (Redwood) — MAP updates, scheduling, stakeholder coordination (ongoing).
- Alex (Acme) — provide evaluation dataset and labeled queries, confirm performance targets and any PII constraints (by 6/18).
- Priya (Acme) — confirm security/data handling requirements and whether tests must run in a VPC/private environment (by 6/18).

Dependencies & gating items:
- Access to anonymized evaluation dataset (Acme).
- Temporary eval keys and firewall/VPN access if tests must run against a private deployment.
- SOC2 report / data handling statement for private VPC evaluation.

Success criteria for go/no-go recommendation (summary):
- At least one model/config meets relevance target (>= +10% MRR or parity with baseline) AND meets p95 latency target for chosen latency profile OR delivers >30% cost improvement while keeping relevance within -5% of baseline.

Next operational steps (this week):
1) Acme shares dataset and confirms whether tests should run in-hosted or in private env (action: Alex/Priya by 6/18).
2) Redwood shares temporary eval keys and the acme-eval-checklist.xlsx (attached) and schedules the benchmark run (action: Rishi by 6/21).
3) Technical kickoff meeting 6/21 to walk through the runbook and assign engineers.

If that looks good I’ll start the runs as soon as we have the dataset and API access.

—Rishi
